trust_decision.summary: Who may reach the Rsdoctor report server (HTTP API, static client, open-in-editor, WebSocket API): at the pinned commit nobody decides. It listens on all interfaces, sends wildcard CORS and accepts any WS handshake. The fix restricts it to loopback bind + local Host header + local Origin + per-server WS token, all decided in RsdoctorServer.bootstrap and Socket.bootstrap.

landing_point.why: The advisory names an unauthenticated HTTP API. The obvious place is the wildcard cors() middleware and the Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* headers in wrapNextHandleFunction (index.ts:203-204) in RsdoctorServer.bootstrap.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about the HTTP API and CORS. The WebSocket handshake ('a separate realtime channel the browser can't read cross-origin anyway'), the generic createServer util in another package, and a server created with noServer:true or disableClientServer:true ('no server is supposed to run') all look outside it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Several legitimate local clients must keep working. The MCP helper in @rsdoctor/ai POSTs to http://localhost:<port> from Node with no Origin and no token. bundle-diff runs two servers on different ports and the client loads across ports (the fix's tests allow 127.0.0.1:port+1). *.localhost origins must also keep working, as must the user-configurable server.cors. Requiring a token on all HTTP, or rejecting every Origin, breaks these.
